title: K8s Compromised Node API Redirect (CVE-2020-8559) — Node-to-Master Privilege Escalation via Proxy
description: CVE-2020-8559 (CVSS 6.4) affects Kubernetes kubelet versions prior to v1.20.x. The vulnerability lies in the node proxy subresource — an authenticated user with node proxy access can redirect the kube-apiserver's exec/attach/portforward requests to any pod in the cluster, bypassing namespace isolation. Attack: (1) Obtain a ServiceAccount token with node proxy permissions (typically a node-operator or cluster-admin SA token). Verify permissions: kubectl auth can-i get nodes and kubectl auth can-i create pods/exec. (2) Discover the target node name: NODE_NAME=$(kubectl get node -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'). (3) List pods on the node via node proxy: curl -k -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://kubernetes.default.svc/api/v1/nodes/${NODE_NAME}/proxy/pods". (4) Identify the victim pod in the target namespace. (5) Use the node proxy to exec into the victim pod (CVE-2020-8559 redirect): kubectl --token=$TOKEN exec -n secure-ns victim-pod -- cat /flag.txt. Key insights: (a) The vulnerability is that node proxy does not validate the target pod's namespace — an attacker with node proxy access can exec into pods in any namespace. (b) The attacker does not need direct pod exec permissions in the target namespace — node proxy access is sufficient. (c) This is a node-to-master escalation: compromising any node or obtaining a node-operator SA token leads to cross-namespace code execution.
indicators: ServiceAccount with node proxy permissions (get nodes, create pods/exec)
Node-operator or cluster-admin SA token accessible
Victim pod in isolated namespace reachable via node proxy
prerequisites: ServiceAccount token with get nodes and create pods/exec permissions
kubectl or curl for API requests
